description: Peat extent for Indonesia from the GFW global peatland extent, a composite: for Indonesia the union of Miettinen et al. 2016 and Gumbricht et al. 2017, rasterised or resampled to 30 m; taken at zoom 11 (about 76 m) for the tiles that touch a KHG: 1 = peat, 0 = no peat, 255 = tile not fetched
source: Global Forest Watch tile cache tiles.globalforestwatch.org/gfw_peatlands/v20230315/is (CC BY 4.0), fetched 2026-10-22 with repeat_common.fetch_peat_extent
year: GFW layer version v20230315 (dates of the source maps not recorded here)
remarks: Only tiles touching a KHG are filled (everything else is 255). A mapped extent, not a survey. The union means the peat area can exceed either source alone; the Miettinen paper covers Peninsular Malaysia, Sumatra and Borneo, so Papua rests on Gumbricht et al. 2017 (modelled). Partially transparent edge cells count as peat (alpha > 0): fully opaque cells only would give about 6% less (24 tiles sampled). About 20-30 points above the 1 km Global Peatland Map in median KHG peat share, per island: see the report. Full-resolution download needs a free GFW API key. Used to count fire on peat and for peat area per KHG.

description: Global Peatland Map 2.0: peat extent, global, about 1 km (1 = peat dominated, 2 = peat in a soil mosaic, 255 = none)
